thread:
Maya Patel: morning shift-bridge, quick summary of overnight noise and customer impact so the day team can pick up. TL;DR: KV cache eviction storm 02:50-04:10 UTC causing 429s for long-context requests (seq>8k) in eu-west. Two paying customers reported degraded throughput (AcmeCorp, Medlytics). See incident INC-2026-311 mentioned by the paging bot below.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: incident INC-2026-311 created and paged at 2026-03-14T02:55:23Z; severity=P2; channel=#eng-oncall; runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction

Arslan Khan: I got the page, ran the quick mitigation steps from the runbook. Short summary of actions I took:
- disabled large-context batching for eu-west (temp)
- increased KV cache slab allocation on pool-3 by +20% (manual)
- added routing fallback to model-small-v2 for requests with seq>9k

Jess Rivera: Logs show a sharp KV miss spike starting ~02:48 UTC. Attaching a minimal log snippet:
```
[02:48:11] kv_cache_eviction: pool=pool-3 misses=1248 evictions=847 hit_rate=12%
[02:49:03] batcher: queued=312 latency_p95=420ms
[02:50:05] http: 429 from runner-7 (kv cache pressure)
```

Maya Patel: Customer impact notes: AcmeCorp observed 40% increase in tail latency and ~15% request errors between 02:50-03:30 UTC (they call this "premium inference" traffic). Medlytics had intermittent failures for long-document embeddings (seq>10k). Both teams were notified by support; no data leakage.

Arslan Khan: Current status as of last check (04:00 UTC): pressure reduced, 429s down to baseline, routing fallback still active. I left a temporary throttle on large-context pipelines to avoid re-trigger. I think we can de-escalate to maintenance but keep eyes on backlog for next 6h.

SRE Rotation: Noted coverage gap: no eu-west secondary on-duty between 03:00-05:00 UTC due to shift swap error. That's why Arslan had to handle solo for 40m. Need to document and fix rotation overlap.

Maya Patel: Action items / recommended next steps for day team:
- (P0) Create an automated alert for "kv eviction rate > 500/min AND hit_rate < 20%" (Pager rule) — owners: eng-runtime / alerting team.
- (P1) Run a controlled repro in staging to validate slab sizing heuristics (runbook step 4). Ticket: RDW-4257.
- (P1) Remove routing fallback after ensuring stable hit rate for 2 hours; rollback steps in runbook.
- (P2) Patch rotation schedule to ensure eu-west has primary+secondary overlap 03:00-05:00 UTC. Ops doc: https://redwood.internal/rotations

Jess Rivera: I'm adding a short checklist to the runbook with exact commands I used to inspect metrics and increase slab allocation. Example commands: 
```
# check eviction metrics
curl -s http://metrics.internal/kv?pool=pool-3 | jq '.evictions_per_min, .hit_rate'
# bump slab (manual temporary)
kubectl exec -n platform cache-controller -- bin/cachectl --pool pool-3 --slab +20
```

Arslan Khan: Notes for whoever takes follow-up: do not increase slab beyond +30% without capacity review (see notes in runbook). If evictions resume after rolling back fallback, immediately re-enable small-model routing and page infra oncall.

Maya Patel: Customer comms: Support drafted messages for AcmeCorp and Medlytics; sent at 03:40 UTC (no SLA breach recorded but need post-incident note). Please coordinate if we decide to proactively offer credits.

SRE Rotation: Handoff: I'm primary until 12:00 UTC, Maya will be secondary then. Arslan — thanks for the rapid response; please stay reachable for 2h in case slab sizing needs follow-up.

Maya Patel: leaving these follow-up subtasks in RDW board: RDW-4257 (repro), RDW-4258 (pager rule), RDW-4259 (rotation overlap fix), RDW-4260 (runbook clarity).

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-311 marked as mitigated at 04:12:09Z by Arslan Khan; status=mitigated; next_update=2026-03-14T08:00:00Z

Jess Rivera: I'll draft the post-incident notes with timelines and include the metric graphs. Expect PR for runbook changes today.

Maya Patel: OK — that's it from me. Primary: SRE Rotation. Secondary: Maya Patel (after 12:00 UTC). Leave any follow-ups here or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
